title: Edit a strategy — compose, compile, review, apply

data.name: strategy
data.shape: Strategy — { id, name, tagline, revision, boundAgentCount }

data.name: proposal
data.shape: { kind: 'proposal' | 'refused', proposal?: { confirmationToken, consequence }, reason?: string }

components.purpose: Compose a change to a strategy, ask BattleGrid what it would do, and decide from the answer.

actions.effect: GET ?tagline=… — compiles and replaces the compose form with the review. Writes nothing.
Server action: applies the reviewed plan, reconfigures bound agents, redirects to /strategies

components.current_implementation: Server component with seven render branches, each a full-page <main> on the shared shell from DT-0001. Page headings at type.size.2xl — raised from xl when rendering DT-0002 showed h1 and the panel h2 were the same size. The compose branch is a method=get form with a single tagline input; only the tagline is editable today (backlog `strategy-section-editor`).
constraints: The compile control must keep saying what it does and does not do — 'Compile — see what this would do, without doing it'. Compiling is effect-free by platform design precisely so a human can look first; a label that reads like a save button gives that back
The bound-agent count must appear above the field on the compose branch, before the user edits — not only on the review
Compiling is a GET and must stay one: shareable, re-runnable by URL, and never a POST that implies commitment
vocabulary-unavailable must remain a full-page refusal, not a dismissible banner over a usable form — composing without the vocabulary means guessing at values the platform will reject

compile-rejected must keep the sentence 'Nothing was changed.' — after a failure the user's first question is whether it was partial. BattleGrid's reason is shown verbatim and usually names what to fix
review-apply-refused still renders the full review; the refusal reason usually names what to change, and hiding the review would strand the user

components.purpose: Show exactly what applying would do, and let the user apply from inside that review rather than beside it.

actions.effect: POSTs the reviewed plan and its confirmation token. Reconfigures every bound agent immediately, then redirects to /strategies.
Returns to the compose form to change the intent
Applies the reviewed plan; reconfigures bound agents immediately; redirects to /strategies
Link back to the compose form

components.current_implementation: Styled per DT-0002. Consequence-toned blast radius with a 4px left border, notice-toned concerns block that shares no colour with danger, quiet-toned summary, accent (not danger) apply button with 'Go back and change it' as a bordered peer. Refusal states render no control at all.
constraints: There must be no control on this surface that applies without a review having been rendered first. Applying is an act performed *from* a review, never a button beside a compile button — two similar controls side by side make the mistake one click wide with a fleet-sized consequence (design S-G)
'Nothing has changed yet' must remain the first thing read. It is the sentence that makes an effect-free compile legible as effect-free
The apply button's label carries the consequence ('reconfigures N agents now') and must not be shortened to a bare verb

Concerns are advisory and must never be presented as blockers — they describe the strategy's existing configuration, the user cannot fix them from here, and treating them as blockers would refuse ordinary edits with no way around it

The BattleGrid-authored `consequence` string is stored with the token so the audit can prove what was shown; it must be displayed verbatim and must not be paraphrased, truncated, or collapsed behind a disclosure
The review must still render when apply is refused — the reason usually names what to change
[concerns-panel] The disclaimer sentence ('These do not prevent the change. They describe how the strategy is set up.') must not be dropped or demoted — without it the panel reads as a blocker
[concerns-panel] Must not adopt error styling. A one-word tagline edit can return two concerns while viable is true; styling them as failures would train users to abandon valid edits
[concerns-panel] Count in the heading must stay, so the user knows the list is complete

[apply-confirmation] The hidden `plan` field carries the reviewed plan rather than recompiling — 'what is applied is what was reviewed' is a requirement, not an aspiration. A design must not move, defer, or re-derive this value
[apply-confirmation] The blocked and not-viable states are role=alert paragraphs that replace the button entirely; there must be no disabled-looking apply control that suggests retrying will help
[apply-confirmation] 'Go back and change it' must remain a visible peer of Apply, not a hidden or tertiary escape — it is the expected outcome of a review that surprised the user

components.purpose: State how many agents this change reaches, as its own claim rather than a clause in a sentence.
components.current_implementation: Three visually distinct treatments. reaches-agents: consequence block, count at type.size.xl/semibold on its own line. reaches-none: a single quiet line, no border, no fill. unknown: notice block, deliberately block-shaped so it cannot be mistaken for zero.
constraints: Must stay its own block. Five bound agents is a different act from zero and must not have to be read for — folding it into a sentence is the specific failure this component exists to prevent
`null` (BattleGrid did not report) must remain visibly distinct from `0` (nothing is bound). Rendering the unknown case as zero would understate the risk
The note that open positions are reported for awareness and do not block must stay with the count

components.purpose: List what would actually differ, and say plainly when nothing would.
components.current_implementation: Heading plus a disc list; a single sentence when the list is empty.
constraints: The empty case must keep its own sentence ('Nothing — this plan leaves the strategy as it is') rather than rendering an empty list; a compile that changes nothing is a real and useful outcome
The proposed revision number is what the user will see on the roster afterwards and must stay legible next to the changes

components.purpose: Turn away a request that has no authority, and say how to fix it.
components.current_implementation: Shared component rendered in place of the page body.
constraints: One page for every cause; they differ in cause and not in remedy (design W-C)

steps: open editor, read blast radius above the field
read 'Nothing has changed yet', blast radius, changed axes, concerns

flows.name: Compile, then think better of it

accessibility.notes: Review section is labelled by `review-heading`. Blast radius, the consequence sentence, and both refusal states are role=alert; the plan summary is role=status. Compiling is a full page navigation, so the review is reached by normal document order rather than a live region.
